title: Statistics - Lesson 2: Quartiles Assessment
description: Assessment for calculating and interpreting Q1, Q2, and Q3 from ungrouped data.

questions.question: Which statement best describes quartiles?
options: They divide ordered data into four parts with about the same number of values
They show only the most common value
They measure the total of all data values
They divide a circle into four equal angles
questions.explanation: Quartiles are position measures that split ordered data into four roughly equal parts.

questions.question: Order the data 18, 10, 14, 22, 16 and enter Q2. Enter just the number.
questions.explanation: The ordered data are 10, 14, 16, 18, 22. The middle value is 16, so Q2 = 16.

questions.question: For the ordered data 10, 14, 16, 18, 22, what are Q1 and Q3 using this lesson's method?
questions.explanation: Exclude Q2 = 16. The lower half is 10, 14, so Q1 = 12. The upper half is 18, 22, so Q3 = 20.

questions.question: For the ordered data 5, 8, 11, 13, 17, 20, 24, 29, what is Q2? Enter just the number.
questions.explanation: There are eight values, so Q2 is the average of 13 and 17: (13 + 17) / 2 = 15.

questions.question: For the ordered data 5, 8, 11, 13, 17, 20, 24, 29, which values are Q1 and Q3?
options: Q1 = 8 and Q3 = 24

questions.question: For an odd number of data values, this lesson includes Q2 in both halves when finding Q1 and Q3.
questions.explanation: This lesson excludes Q2 from both halves when the total number of values is odd.

questions.question: A data set of running times has Q3 = 18 minutes. Which interpretation is best?
options: About 75% of the running times are at or below 18 minutes
Every runner finished in exactly 18 minutes
18 minutes is the longest running time
About 25% of the running times are at or below 18 minutes
questions.explanation: Q3 marks the point where about three-fourths of the data are at or below that value.

questions.question: For the ordered data 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, what is Q1? Enter just the number.
questions.explanation: Q2 is 8, so exclude it. The lower half is 2, 4, 6, and its median is 4.

questions.question: For the ordered data 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, what is Q3? Enter just the number.
questions.explanation: Q2 is 8, so exclude it. The upper half is 10, 12, 14, and its median is 12.

questions.question: Which error would most likely lead to incorrect quartiles?
options: Finding Q1 and Q3 before ordering the data
Writing a sentence after calculating
Checking whether the number of values is odd or even
Labeling Q2 as the median
questions.explanation: Quartiles depend on ordered positions, so using unordered data can place the halves incorrectly.

questions.question: A student says, "Q1 is 42, so 42 is the smallest value." Explain the mistake.
questions.correctAnswer: Q1 is not the minimum; it is the median of the lower half, so about 25% of the data are at or below 42.
questions.explanation: The minimum is the smallest value. Q1 is a quartile boundary inside the ordered data set.

questions.question: Explain how to find Q1, Q2, and Q3 for a data set with an even number of values.
questions.correctAnswer: Order the data, average the two middle values to find Q2, then find the median of the lower half for Q1 and the median of the upper half for Q3.
questions.explanation: For an even number of values, the two halves are formed naturally after the middle pair is used to find Q2.

questions.question: The five-number summary of a data set is 6, 11, 15, 23, 31. What is Q2?
questions.explanation: A five-number summary is minimum, Q1, Q2, Q3, maximum. The third value is Q2.

questions.question: If two data sets have the same median, they must also have the same Q1 and Q3.
questions.explanation: The median only describes the center. The lower and upper halves can differ, so Q1 and Q3 can be different.

questions.question: A set of project scores has Q1 = 68, Q2 = 80, and Q3 = 91. Write a complete interpretation of these quartiles.
questions.correctAnswer: About 25% of the project scores are at or below 68, about 50% are at or below 80, and about 75% are at or below 91.
questions.explanation: A complete interpretation connects each quartile to the approximate percent of project scores at or below that value.
